findings.title: effect_pan clamps the pan TARGET at the LIVE zoom, not cam_zoom_to - a drag during any zoom ease (incl. the 1.5-2 s pullback window) converges outside the world clamp or destroys an in-flight zoom-to-point anchor
findings.location: app/main.odin effect_pan (camera_pan_center + camera_clamp_center both take app.cam_zoom)
findings.detail: Targets converge at cam_zoom_to but are validated at the eased cam_zoom; camera_update never re-clamps. Zooming out 2.0->1.0 with a pan to cy=585 (valid at 2.0) converges showing world y [195,975] - a 195px cut-off band plus void (the exact B1 failure shape, via the pan path). Zooming in at the fit: the 1.0 clamp pins the target center to the world center and overwrites the wheel's off-center anchor target.
findings.fix: In effect_pan pass cam_zoom_to to camera_clamp_center (keep the live zoom for the camera_pan_center delta per W5); optionally pin a mid-ease pan value test.

findings.title: Release-build wheel dead-zone: the ungated D-key sets overlay_on, and camera_wheel_policy then routes ~23% of the window to a compiled-out Noc_Scroll body
findings.location: app/input/mouse.odin:173 (D mapping, ungated) + app/main.odin:964 effect_overlay (ungated) + app/main.odin:1704 effect_zoom
findings.detail: effect_overlay's comment claims 'the toggle + the draw are compile-gated' but only the DRAW is; mouse.odin has zero PP_DEBUG gates. Release: D sets overlay_on (invisible), camera_wheel_policy returns .Noc_Scroll over the 360x600 panel rect, effect_zoom's PP_DEBUG-gated body is a bare return - the wheel silently dies with no visible cause.
findings.fix: Compile-gate the D mapping (or the Toggle_Overlay exec case / effect_overlay) under PP_DEBUG so release can never set overlay_on.

findings.title: The W4 pin is vacuous vs the r2 skew mode: the router is placed BEFORE the seed, so the newest-terminal walk takes the seed without ever traversing the router - the kind filter is unexercised
findings.detail: r2 W4's skew required the router to hold a NEWER id than the seed (the old count walk-back then pointed at the router). Here the seed is newest, so both the old and new walks map it correctly - deleting the Terminal filter keeps this test green.
findings.fix: Swap the order: spawn the seed WITH its event, then place_router, then feed - the walk must traverse and skip the junction to find the seed.

findings.title: pullback_yields test drives effect_settings_adjust on a zeroed App - settings_save_app falls back to the real HOME dotfile and writes the dev's settings (auto_pullback OFF) on every native test run
findings.detail: settings_save_app's own comment says 'a test must never touch it'; the zeroed fixture has settings_path_override == "" so the adjust persists to the real ~/.pp-settings.bin. Deterministic, not 'may'.
findings.fix: Set app7.settings_path_override to a temp path (the exec-level adjust-test pattern) before the toggle.

findings.title: pullback_feed caps the spawn-event mapping at 8 ids - a 9+ spawn frame silently returns and skips the pullback
findings.detail: camera_newest_terminals stops at len(ids)=8; a genuine seed in a large catch-up burst never pulls back, silently. Unreachable via current data (interval 80 ticks vs the 5-tick frame cap) but interval is balance.json data.
findings.fix: Size the buffer to the max same-frame spawns or clamp n_spawns to the buffer and map the OLDEST 8 (the newest-first walk order makes a truncated mapping still correct for the newest seed).

findings.title: The W7 same-window exclusion's correctness silently depends on terminal_spawn_interval_ticks exceeding the 5-tick frame cap - an unstated data invariant nothing asserts
findings.detail: At interval <= 5 two spawns land in one frame; the core's second plan then sees the first spawn live, but the frame-level exclusion hides it - the view classification diverges from plan-time (false SEEDs). Inert today, wrong when the data moves.
findings.fix: Assert the invariant where balance loads (interval > max ticks/frame), or derive the exclusion window from the interval instead of the frame slice.

findings.title: Wheel zoom band clamp [1.0, 4.0] has no pin on the wheel path - clamp-removal regressions pass every test
findings.detail: Acceptance says 'wheel zoom-to-point, clamped'; no test drives camera_zoom_at/effect_zoom at the 4.0 ceiling or 1.0 floor (the existing test even sidesteps: delta -1 'a +1 notch would clamp').
findings.fix: One pin: from zoom 4.0 a +4 wheel holds 4.0; from 1.0 a -4 wheel holds 1.0 (targets unchanged).

findings.title: The W5 fold (pan converts against the live zoom) is untested - effect_pan has zero value assertions, the exact seam where R3-B1 lives
findings.detail: The fixture sits mid-ease (cam_zoom=4.0 vs cam_zoom_to lower) yet no assertion reads cam_wx_to/cam_wy_to after effect_pan; both the live-vs-target regression and the clamp application are unpinned.
findings.fix: Assert the pan target equals center - dx/(fit*live_zoom) clamped at the TARGET zoom, mid-ease.

findings.title: Pullback ease-rate band (~1.5-2 s ruling) weakly pinned - a 0.14-rate regression (0.66 s convergence, outside the ruled band) passes
findings.detail: After 30 frames the residual gap at rate 0.14 (~0.021) still exceeds the 0.005 snap threshold, so 'still in flight' holds for both rates; CAMERA_PULLBACK_EASE could regress to the normal rate undetected.
findings.fix: Pin the rate band numerically: gap after N frames within the 0.05-rate envelope (e.g. gap_30 in [0.35, 0.45] of the initial gap).

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS - P0 100%, P1 ~87% (34/39), overall ~86%
findings.detail: All three r2 blocker folds pinned at P0; P1 gaps: wheel clamp band (W5), effect_pan values (W6), ease-rate band (W7), the vacuous W4 pin + newest_terminals edges. P1 sits in the 80-89% CONCERNS band.
findings.fix: Close W4-W7 above; the gate returns to PASS.

findings.title: Stale-latch guard can synthesize a Mouse_Release every frame when placement is armed while the pan latch is stranded
findings.location: app/input/poll.odin poll_mouse + app/input/mouse.odin pan branch (placing_eff < 0 gate)
findings.detail: The synthetic release only clears the latch via the pan branch, which requires placing_eff < 0; with placement armed nothing clears it - a release is appended every frame (and a synthetic release into the placement branch risks an unwanted placement commit).
findings.fix: Clear inp.panning in the stale-guard branch itself (the synthesized release's purpose is closing the latch), before appending.

findings.title: camera_pullback_target comment 'at any z_to the clamp is a no-op for a zoom-out' is contradicted by the diff's own B1 pin (cy 585->390 at z_to=1.0)
findings.detail: The clamp demonstrably moves the center on a zoom-out in the floor case (viewport >= world pins to the world center). The code is right; the comment's mechanism is wrong.
findings.fix: Reword: the clamp is a no-op for a zoom-out EXCEPT at the fit floor, where it pins - which is the B1 contract.

findings.title: PR body's verification counts stale (r2 N2's exact class, unclaimed): claims 4+4+4 new pins, the diff's own new files contain 9+7+7 (+2 settings)
findings.detail: All four test files are new in this diff; @(test) counts are 9 (camera_test), 7 (camera_input_test), 7 (pullback_test), 2 new settings. Understates coverage but misleads audits - the third round of drifted counts.
findings.fix: Update the PR body to 9+7+7+2 (25 new pins).

findings.title: W10 fold leaves start_run's pan-latch reset untested - r2 W10 explicitly asked to assert it
findings.detail: The lifecycle test pins release, begin_draw, modal, and the suppress branch; deleting the start_run reset keeps every gate green.
findings.fix: One app-level pin: arm the latch, call start_run, assert panning == false.

findings.title: N1's 'ONE source' fit claim still false: the derivation lives in both main's camera_fit and render's view_compute
findings.detail: r2 N1's triplication became a duplication (camera_update now calls camera_fit), but view_compute still inlines min(sx, sy) - render cannot import main, so the comment overclaims while two sources must move in lockstep.
findings.fix: Export a render-side camera_fit helper (view_compute + main both call it) or soften the comment to name view_compute as the second site.

findings.title: touch.odin header still documents Pan as 'a deliberate no-op in the executor today' - the superseded 5.4 comment this job claims to have replaced
findings.detail: types.odin's Pan comment, exec.odin, and parity.odin were updated; touch.odin's header copy was missed and now contradicts the routing.
findings.fix: Reword the header to route-pan wording matching types.odin.

findings.title: cam_test_ctx heap-allocates the View (new(rnd.View)) and never deletes it - destroy() frees only events/intents
findings.detail: Every other fixture buffer is explicitly freed; the heap View leaks per test run (the N6 fold added the catalogs defers but missed this).
findings.fix: defer delete(ictx.view) in each test (or stack-allocate into a var the Input references).

findings.title: 'four constants' ungated - five NOC constants (X/Y/W/H/ROW_H) sit outside the PP_DEBUG gate
findings.detail: The comment says 'four constants + two tiny procs'; NOC_ROW_H rides along ungated (plus the Wheel_Target enum). Trivial, but comments that miscount invite drift audits.
findings.fix: Either move NOC_ROW_H back inside the gate or fix the comment to five + enum.

findings.title: Pan executor has no draw guard - a two-finger touch pan fires mid-draw, unlike the mouse path (!drag_eff gate)
findings.detail: mouse_map emits Pan only when no draw is active; the executor routes every Pan intent unconditionally, so a second finger during a touch draw pans the camera mid-gesture (preview re-snaps; commit uses node ids, so worst case is jitter).
findings.fix: Decide + document: either suppress Pan while inp.drag.active in the executor or declare the co-fire intentional in the comment.

findings.title: Wheel residue advances before the ownership decision - NOC-scrolled/modal-blocked wheels pre-charge the accumulator a notch
findings.detail: Residue consumed as Noc_Scroll/Blocked persists (the only write is the poll); the first map scrolling after leaving the panel fires one notch early. Cosmetic bias, never a spontaneous zoom (residue only fires with new w != 0).
findings.fix: Reset wheel_accum to 0 when the policy consumes a notch as Noc_Scroll or Blocked (or accept + document the carry).

findings.title: camera_newest_terminals has no direct unit pin - the found<n bail, >8 spawns, dead-id skip, and event<->id ordering are unpinned
findings.detail: The only coverage is the feed-level walk test - which (per R3-W1) never even traverses the router. The walk is the W4 fix's core; its edges deserve direct pins.
findings.fix: Direct unit pins on camera_newest_terminals: interleaved junction AFTER the terminal (the real skew), 0-found, dead ids, newest-first order.

findings.title: PR-body claim 'a second SEED mid-ease retargets it' has no test
findings.detail: A claimed behavior of the ruling's implementation is unpinned: a regression that early-outs when pullback is already armed would pass all tests.
findings.fix: Arm a pullback, spawn a farther seed, feed again, assert the targets moved to the second district.

findings.title: poll_mouse wheel seam (w != 0 gate, residue persistence, notch emission) untested - acceptable raylib boundary
findings.detail: Reads live raylib state, untestable without device injection; the pure accumulator and the chain above the seam are pinned. Consistent with the repo's untested poll seam.
findings.fix: None required (documented acceptance).

findings.title: W4 pin's fixture-id comments are wrong: claims 'id 6'/'id 7', actual ids are 3 and 4 (run_init spawns no fixture nodes)
findings.detail: run_init only zero-inits state (no spawns); the fixture's explicit spawns give router=3, seed=4. Assertions are id-agnostic so the pin still bites (its vacuousness is R3-W1), but the comments mislead - the N4 disease again.
findings.fix: Fix the comments (or drop the ids).
